$comment: S5 blind solve - ccao-f round 1. exam-examiner (fresh session, never authored this bank), 2026-08-18. Protocol: methodology/05-eval-rubric.md #blind-solve. The keyless form (stems + options only, ids preserved, nothing shuffled) was generated from questions.json with a script that projected only id/type/question/options; every answer, confidence grade and reasoning line below was written and frozen to disk BEFORE the key, any rationale, any distractor_patterns tag or any concept metadata was read. One documented exception is flagged on ccao-f-d1-q01. Result: 81/81 match, zero misses, therefore zero adjudications open. Cross-model matrix: none - the Codex advisory instrument was unavailable (eval/codex-solve.json).

cue_analysis.$comment: A 100% blind pass is itself a signal, so the surface cues that could produce one without concept knowledge were measured. Findings feed dimension 5 and the Gate 2 notes; none is a bounce on its own.

key_position_single_choice.reading: perfectly balanced across 72 SC items - the aif-c01 BD-1 defect does not recur

cue_analysis.key_pairs_multiple_response: all 9 MR items carry a distinct key pair (AB AC AD AE BD BE CD CE DE) - no repeated pair to learn

answer_length.reading: a mild statistical lean toward the key being the longest option. The margin is ~7 characters on ~100-character options, well below a readable cue, so this is a watch item (cf. LEARNING.md L-0021 on aif-c01's mirror-image key-shortest lean), not a defect. Recorded so a future authoring wave does not widen it.

cue_analysis.pattern_shape_cue: 31 items carry exactly one, and 6 items carry two, distractors from the 'eliminable by shape' family (D14 dogma / D16 refuse-the-mandate / D19 false-technical-claim). The 6 two-of-three items (d2-q27, d3-q35, d3-q36, d3-q38, d5-q56, d6-q70) were scored down on dimension 5 or 2 where the shape actually did the work; see judge-scores.json.
cue_analysis.e02_family_cue: E02 fluency-as-evidence appears on 20 distractors (8.2%, cap 0.15). A candidate who learns the single rule 'the option that praises polish/confidence is never the key' gets those 20 eliminations free. This is legitimate - fluency-is-not-accuracy is a core blueprint theme and the vendor's own samples use it - but it is the largest single learnable cue in the bank, and it is why the examiner's confidence ran high on so many items. Gate 2 note, not a bounce.

items.reasoning: Fitness for the business purpose is the only standard that survives; register, length and peer endorsement are all proxies.
items.independence_note: NON-INDEPENDENT: this item's full record (answer + rationale) was visible during schema discovery, before the keyless form was generated. The blind result is recorded for completeness but carries no evidential weight; the item is auto-added to the Gate 2 sample.

items.reasoning: The two failures are a length breach and a shape breach, so the two missing prompt components are constraints and output format.
Generic output with the differentiating detail sitting outside the request is a missing-context failure, not a capability ceiling.
One opaque prompt doing three jobs cannot be diagnosed; ordered steps with a check between them localise the failure.
Build and verify the step everything downstream depends on first; client eagerness does not change the dependency order.
Three functions in one pass hides which function errs; separate stages give each function its own checkable result.
The draft is a diagnostic pointing at the length constraint; change that one component instead of rewriting everything.
Five rounds of wording cannot supply data that was never attached; the missing component is the sales figures.
Definitions have stopped paying; labelled borderline examples are the component that teaches the boundary.
Strategy must match task type: constraints suit analysis, deliberate latitude suits ideation.
Current duty rates are a research task; prompting it as drafting produced polished prose with no grounding.
The three references (requirements, source material, professional standards) apply to every draft; only depth of review scales with stakes.
Every stated claim being true says nothing about omissions; completeness against the decision's needs is the unchecked axis.
Accountability stays with the person whose name is on the letter; disclosure and routing do not transfer it.
Self-reported confidence is not evidence; a cited return and a regulatory date must be validated against authoritative sources.
Plausible is not verified; load-bearing claims need authoritative records regardless of how confident the model says it is.
A systematic framing pattern passing review means the review lacks a bias dimension; add it to the routine check.
Volatile, recently revised rules must be supplied or retrieved from a current authoritative source, then the answer validated against them.
Request-time protections: bound claims to the uploaded pack with citations, and license an explicit 'I don't know'; the fact-check is a later control, not a prompt provision.
Decision-grade numbers should be computed from the export by code, not generated as prose.
The review threshold is set by stakes/reversibility and audience/regulatory exposure - not by fluency, tier or deadline.
Mandatory review means a reviewer competent on the requirement with the records needed to check it; a tone skim is not review.
Adaptation must preserve claims; the qualifier that dropped changed the claim, so that statistic is re-verified.
Set the criterion before reading so the comparison is against requirements, not fluency or popularity.
Re-keying errors are a format-reliability problem; structured data the system ingests removes the transcription step.
The evaluation sample was written for the trial; it must be rebuilt from real, messy, contradictory contracts.
Variation is inherent, so the answer is structural review plus a measured consistency bound, not a defect report or withdrawal.
A safety-contact error is a stop condition; thresholds are not averages when one class of error is categorical.
Recurring task with fixed reference material is a Project-shaped task; pick the entry point from task shape before writing the prompt.
Needs current published information from many external sources - that is the research surface.
Twice a quarter with a human reviewer does not justify an automated pipeline; delegate deliberately.
A Skill makes the procedure repeatable; code execution makes the totals computed rather than plausible.
High-volume extraction to the light tier, everyday work to the mid tier, hardest strategy work to the top tier.
When two tiers clear the bar, the cheapest/fastest that clears it is the right pick for high-volume structured work.
Top tier for everything is a cost and latency tax, not a safety margin; route bulk work down.
A week-long thread exhausts a finite context budget; degradation is the budget, not a swapped model.
Carry the conclusions into a fresh session before the budget bites; the exploratory trail is not needed.
Context window holds the current conversation; Memory is the mechanism that carries anything across sessions.
Requirements analysis: structured, source-traceable, testable requirements - not a readable summary or a whole process design.
Checkability before downstream consumption is the delegation qualifier; repetitiveness and confident-reading output are not.
Plans must be built on verified numbers - compute the totals from the export while the narrative is synthesised.
Nothing is measured, so the target is a guess; instrument first, then aim at the friction the data shows.
Strong drafts are not a reason to remove the checkpoints where human judgment re-enters.
The review named one failing component; iterate on that component rather than restarting.
Delegate steps deliberately and keep the human approval gate; the approval is the step that must not be automated.
Map every step on reversibility, stakes and accountability and give a three-way verdict, not a binary automate/keep.
A gate must sit before the irreversible act and have a named accountable owner; timing out or logging after the fact are not gates.
Fixed steps in a fixed order with fixed validation is a workflow, not an agent; grant autonomy only where it is needed.
The requirement is a template-conformant draft plus duty-officer review; the pipeline adds machinery no requirement asked for.
Durable trust comes from stating limits alongside capabilities and naming the review gates that make reliance safe.
Configuration work is in scope; API integration is a developer boundary - deliver the first and escalate the second.
A weekly recurring task means the one-off setup cost amortises across every later run; configuration is leverage.
Mechanism mismatch: reference data belongs in knowledge, a repeatable procedure belongs in a Skill, instructions govern behaviour.
Reorganising folders and changing permissions is outside the connector's scope; no rewording crosses a capability boundary.
Screen each file for authority/currency with a recorded owner, and scope the upload to the questions asked with a refresh cadence.
Resolve the conflict explicitly by recording which document governs which scope and stating the resolution in replies.
An upload timestamp is file metadata, not content currency; check against the agency's current rules.
A vague standing instruction produces no observable change; rewrite it as precise, testable rules.
Durable rules belong in instructions; uploaded knowledge is data and carries no instruction authority.
Configurations decay silently against a changing world, so maintenance must be scheduled rather than triggered by a signal.
A shared configuration change has downstream consumers; tell the three teams what changed.
The screen is a graded assessment on the delegation criteria, not a yes/no gate; this lands appropriate-with-review.
Governance is a practitioner skill: reason the uncovered case against the policy's boundaries and record the reasoning.
Classify the data against policy first, then match handling - de-identify and scope; deadline pressure does not change the order.
Classification drives handling: strip the regulated identifiers and summarise the redacted file, keeping the work inside policy.
The deciding question is where the data comes to rest on each surface - retention, Memory persistence, connector scope.
Minimise what is logged and bound retention to policy; indefinite logs of account numbers are the defect.
A local risk argument is not an exception; take a documented exception request with compensating controls to the policy owner.
A Skill is software - review its source and requested permissions; install counts and ratings are not an evaluation.
Benchmark the new tier against the current baseline on the same assessments, then stage the change.
Name the boundary, offer the permitted alternative, and log it - refusal without a path, or covert compliance, both fail.
Ambiguous cases are reasoned against the screening criteria and recorded; instinct and another region's precedent are not grounds.
A decision letter owes the student disclosure of AI involvement and a named route to contest the outcome.
Underperformance has discoverable causes; run the diagnostic sequence in order before changing tiers or blaming the tool.
Isolate before you fix - identify which layer failed; that determines which fix is right.
Strong-draft-plus-edit is the realistic ceiling; the mismatch is the promise of mail-ready output, not the prompt.
Three simultaneous changes are unattributable; reintroduce them one at a time from a rebuilt baseline.
A refusal is data: check the request against the task, current policy and permissions, then redo the permitted portion.
Turn vague feedback into one named, testable change rather than a resolution to be careful.
A repeated fix belongs in the configuration - instructions or a Skill - so every scheduler inherits it by default.
A claimed gain needs a reconstructed before measure and the same measures after, on an instrumented workflow.
